review_status: All bytes reviewed; LLVM tests not executed. Implementation of function specialization in Ink remains open.

insights.transfer: LLVM estimates constant propagation/dead-block savings before solver confirmation. Ink ranking may speculate, but emitted specialization and dropped work require ordinary source-bound proofs; cost models never authorize a rewrite.

Group all matching call sites by exact argument/constant signature; do analysis once per signature. Ink keys additionally bind exact core/module, type instantiation, checked effects and knowledge context.

insights.topic: Plan a family before changing calls
insights.transfer: Discover and rank candidates first, create selected clones, then rematch recursive/remaining call sites after propagation. Avoid decision order changing candidate availability.

The heap selects at most eligible-function-count times MaxClones across the module, with explicit index tie-breaking. It is not a strict independent per-function limit. Ink should state and enforce both local and aggregate search/code-growth budgets.
Pending PHIs are retried after all specialized arguments propagate. Distinguish temporarily unknown from definitely unsuitable; retain bounded dependency lists rather than repeating unrelated work.

Transitive PHI walks deduplicate values, cap iterations and incoming fan-in, and reject conflicting constants/unknown non-PHI inputs. Ink recursive summaries need analogous safe widening and termination with fixed semantic proof gates.

KnownConstants and DeadBlocks prevent double counting removed instructions; latency is aggregated only after every argument and pending PHI has been processed. Ink combined transformations need marginal/shared cost accounting.

Compute frequency-weighted latency only after cheaper size/inline gates. Frequency/latency are heuristic estimates: integer weighting drops sub-entry frequencies, and thresholds are LLVM-specific rather than portable constants.

Constant function pointers expose direct calls and future inlining; their bonus is separate and remains speculative. Ink bounded callback unfolding can benefit from composed costing instead of treating each intermediate rewrite as independently profitable.

Growth is accumulated when chosen clones are created. Candidate profitability checks occur earlier; early force/inlining-bonus exits bypass later growth checks. Do not copy these heuristics as hard Ink resource guarantees.

Stack-to-global promotion requires a single nonvolatile store, no unknown users and readonly pointer call use. Ink needs exact ownership, escape/effects and lifecycle proofs before changing storage; observations alone cannot establish readonly.

Cloned return facts reset dependent call lattice values and rerun propagation; removed functions clear cached analyses. Persisting summaries without source/context invalidation can hide newly available constants or keep stale facts.

Exclude interposable/noduplicate/minsize/inlined-away functions, preserve address-taken originals, and reject poison. Ink public/host callbacks remain unconstrained unless exact whole-source authority closes the use set.

insights.topic: Temporary analysis forms interact with later passes
insights.transfer: Predicate no-op copies are removed before clone/stack promotion. Ink analysis forms must have explicit lifetimes so later structural matching does not silently miss equivalent input.

insights.topic: Finer instruction facts as proposal support
insights.transfer: LLVM can estimate calls, loads, GEPs and selects using target semantics. Ink current unsigned expression analysis should expand only with defined supported types/effects and independent checks, never LLVM pointer/undef/poison assumptions.

current_implementation: F063 query-local reuse applied to offline fact discovery, with independent proof replay. This is not interprocedural specialization.
